register.access_notes: COULD NOT REACH THE REGISTER AT ALL on 23 September 2026. Seven attempts from three different clients, spaced 2 seconds or more apart, against four hostnames: (1) curl https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/prefaces/toc with an honest self-identifying user-agent ('canon-legislation-indexer/1.0 (metadata indexing; contact ...)') -> 'curl: (28) Failed to connect to docs.legis.wisconsin.gov port 443 after 21139 ms: Could not connect to server'; (2) curl https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/ -> same timeout; (3) curl https://legis.wisconsin.gov/ -> same; (4) curl https://docs.legis.wi.gov/statutes/statutes/109 -> same; (5) curl https://www.legis.wisconsin.gov/lrb/ -> same; (6) WebFetch of https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/109 -> 'connect ECONNREFUSED 165.189.140.59:443'; (7) navigation in a real browser (the built-in browser pane) -> 'navigation to https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov was denied or failed', with no HTTP response. I also tried plain HTTP on port 80: 'Failed to connect to docs.legis.wisconsin.gov port 80 after 21399 ms'. DNS resolves normally (docs.legis.wisconsin.gov -> 165.189.140.59), so this is a network- or IP-level refusal by the host, not a DNS or client fault. Control fetches of two other registers (code.dccouncil.gov and wyoleg.gov) succeeded from the same clients in the same session, so the problem is specific to the Wisconsin host. I did NOT use a proxy, a cache, a VPN or a spoofed user-agent to get around it, and I did NOT substitute Justia, FindLaw, Casetext, Cornell LII or a Wisconsin agency page as a basis for in-force status. Consequence: 'acts' is deliberately empty and the nine non-federal topics are recorded below as unverified rather than as gaps. A human on a network the register accepts should redo Wisconsin from scratch: the statutes browse at https://docs.legis.wisconsin.gov/statutes/statutes/<chapter>, each chapter page carries its own update stamp, and the likely chapters are 103/104/109 (employment regulations, minimum wage, wage payment), 40 (Wisconsin Retirement System), 49 (public assistance), 108 (unemployment insurance), 71 (income and franchise taxes, with withholding), 628/631 (insurance marketing and the insurance contract), 196 (regulation of public utilities) and 704 (landlord and tenant) alongside 100 (marketing; trade practices) - all UNVERIFIED chapter guesses that must be confirmed against the register itself.

licence.summary: NOT VERIFIED - the register's own copyright or terms page could not be reached (see access_notes), so nothing can be quoted, and open_licence is set false as a placeholder rather than as a finding. What can be said without the register: as a matter of law the text of the Wisconsin Statutes is a government edict and is not subject to copyright (Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org, 590 U.S. 255 (2020)). Wisconsin prepares and publishes its statutes in-house through the Legislative Reference Bureau rather than through a commercial publisher under contract, so no publisher's copyright is expected to sit over the consolidated text itself. Whether the site asserts any rights over the annotations, cross-references, notes, numbering or the site software is UNVERIFIED. A human must read the register's own terms before the corpus relies on any of this.

register.name: Wyoming Legislature, Legislative Service Office - Wyoming Statutes (text-only NXT edition)
register.access_notes: Reachable, but only after finding the right door. https://www.wyoleg.gov/StateStatutes/StatutesConstitution returns HTTP 200 to curl but is an Angular shell with no content in the HTML, so I loaded the LSO site in a real browser (the built-in browser pane, ordinary Chrome, no user-agent spoofing) and read its own navigation. That page offers three routes: 'Wyoming Statutes, Constitution, and Non-Codified Water Laws' -> the LSO's own Rocket NXT (Folio) browser at /NXT/gateway.dll; 'Wyoming Statutes-Files in Download Format' -> one PDF per title at https://wyoleg.gov/statutes/compress/title<NN>.pdf (zero-padded below 10: title01.pdf, title09.pdf); and 'Wyoming Statutes Annotated' -> an off-site LexisNexis-hosted edition at http://www.lexisnexis.com/hottopics/wystatutes/. The NXT browser builds its table of contents from an XML endpoint the page itself calls, gateway.dll?f=xmlcontents&command=getchildren&basepathid=<path>, which returns the infobase tree - title captions, chapter captions, article captions and section catchlines - as metadata. I used that endpoint with curl and an honest self-identifying user-agent ('canon-legislation-indexer/1.0 (metadata indexing; contact ...)'), about 25 requests spaced 1-2 seconds apart, plus about 6 browser page loads. Everything returned HTTP 200 first time. No 403, no 429, no bot challenge, no CAPTCHA, no rate limiting. https://wyoleg.gov/robots.txt returns a 404 page, so the site publishes no crawl rules. I read only the contents tree, never a section document, so no statute text was copied; the per-title PDFs were confirmed to exist by HEAD request only. Note for a later pass: the NXT root offers seven separate infobases (2026, 2025, 2024, 2023, 2022, 2021 and 2020 Wyoming Statutes); everything below is from the 2026 one.

licence.summary: Open in substance, but stated nowhere. The LSO site carries no copyright notice, no terms-of-use page and no licence of any kind - the footer links are Home, About the Legislature, Legislative Service Office, Contact Us, Disclaimer and Privacy Policy, and the Disclaimer page asserts no rights at all; it only disclaims official status and accuracy. Nothing on the register restricts reuse or adaptation. Under the US government edicts doctrine (Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org, 590 U.S. 255 (2020)) the text of the Wyoming Statutes as enacted is not copyrightable, so reuse and adaptation are lawful. TWO WARNINGS. (1) The free text-only edition is expressly NOT the official record: 'The information obtained from this site is not the official record, nor intended to replace the official record, of the Wyoming Legislature.' (2) The ANNOTATED edition is commercial and restricted: the LSO's own Statutes page says 'The online version of the Wyoming Statutes Annotated is provided for non-commercial use pursuant to a contractual arrangement with LexisNexis and will be updated quarterly.' That non-commercial restriction attaches to the LexisNexis-hosted annotated edition and its annotations - not to the LSO's own text-only statutes - but it means the corpus should take its Wyoming text from the LSO NXT edition or the LSO title PDFs, never from the LexisNexis site.

Ann. tit. 27, ch. 4 (ss 27-4-101 through 27-4-508), comprising art. 1 In General (27-4-101 to 27-4-116), art. 2 Minimum Wages (27-4-201 to 27-4-204), art. 3 Equal Pay (27-4-301 to 27-4-304), art. 4 Prevailing Wages (27-4-401 to 27-4-413) and art. 5 Collection of Unpaid Wages (27-4-501 to 27-4-508)
acts.verified_how: walked the LSO NXT table of contents (gateway.dll?f=xmlcontents&command=getchildren) down to 'TITLE 27 - LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT' > 'CHAPTER 4 - WAGES' and each of its five articles, whose first and last section catchlines read '27-4-101. Semimonthly payments required; method of payment; agricultural operations exempt; payment in case of labor dispute or temporary layoff.' ... '27-4-116. Employee not liable for dishonored check; penalty.'; '27-4-201. Definitions.' ... '27-4-204. Liability for unpaid minimum wage; suit for collection.'; '27-4-301. Definitions.' ... '27-4-304. Penalty for violations.'; '27-4-401. Short title.' ... '27-4-413. Inapplicability and exemptions.'; '27-4-501. Definitions.' ... '27-4-508. Agreements for reciprocal enforcement; of claim to another state.'. Repealed sections are shown in the same listing with a 'Repealed by Laws ...' catchline (e.g. '37-3-103. Repealed by Laws 1995, ch. 192, s 3.'), so the substantive catchlines above are live text. Currency: the LSO's Statutes Download page states 'This version of the Wyoming Statutes contains changes from the 2026 Budget Session and reflects the contents of the statutes as they exist as of July 1, 2026'; the NXT infobase I browsed is the one labelled '2026 Wyoming Statutes' (the register also keeps 2020-2025 as separate historical infobases). acts.notes: Covers pay frequency, method of payment, pay on quitting or discharge (27-4-104 'Payment of employee quitting or discharged and suit for wages; generally', with the penalty at 27-4-105), the state minimum wage, equal pay, prevailing wages on public works, and the Labor Standards route for collecting unpaid wages. Wyoming's own minimum wage in art. 2 sits below the federal floor, so the federal FLSA (29 U.S.C. ch. 8) governs most private employment - worth saying in the subject README.

THE TENANCY HALF OF THIS TOPIC IS A DIFFERENT STATUTE and a human should decide whether to encode it too: residential tenancies sit in Title 1, Chapter 21, Article 12 - Residential Rental Property, ss 1-21-1201 ('Definitions.') through 1-21-1211 ('Owner's remedies; eviction; judicial remedies; damages.'), verified on the register in the same session, with eviction procedure in the adjacent art. 10 Forcible Entry and Detainer and art. 14 Removal of Unauthorized Occupants. Wyoming has no uniform residential landlord and tenant act; art. 12 is short (11 sections) but it is the whole of the state's residential tenancy statute. Consumer credit is separately in Title 40, ch. 14 (Wyoming Uniform Consumer Credit Code).

topic_gaps.reason: No Wyoming statute. I walked the whole of Title 27 (Labor and Employment) on the register: its fifteen chapters are General Provisions, Labor and Statistics, Unemployment Compensation, Wages, Hours of Labor, Employment of Women and Children, Labor Unions, Employment Offices and Agencies, Fair Employment Practices, Collective Bargaining for Fire Fighters, Occupational Health and Safety, Worker's Compensation (two chapters), Displaced Worker Education and Training and Presumptive Disability - none of which creates any entitlement to annual, sick, family or holiday leave, paid or unpaid. Chapter 5 (Hours of Labor) is about overtime for state and county employees (27-5-101) and mine working days (27-5-102), with 27-5-103 to 27-5-107 repealed in 1979. Leave for state employees is set by the Wyoming Personnel Rules (regulation) rather than statute, and job-protected family leave comes from the federal FMLA (29 U.S.C. ch. 28). Nothing to list.

No Wyoming statute. Wyoming is an at-will employment state with no severance-pay statute and no mini-WARN mass-layoff notice statute; federal WARN (29 U.S.C. ss 2101-2109) does that work. Title 27, ch. 13 is 'Displaced Worker Education and Training' - retraining funding, not termination rights. The one statutory duty on termination is the timing of final wages, already covered by the Act listed under Payroll/wages (Wyo. Stat. Ann. ss 27-4-104 and 27-4-105, 'Payment of employee quitting or discharged and suit for wages'). Discriminatory discharge is dealt with by Title 27, ch. 9 (Fair Employment Practices), an anti-discrimination statute rather than a termination statute. Nothing to list.

Wyoming levies no individual income tax, so there is no statute to list and no state wage withholding. This is not an assumption: on the register, Title 39 (Taxation and Revenue) ch. 7 'INCOME TAXES' contains exactly one section, '39-7-101. Repealed By Laws 1998, ch. 5, s 4.', and ch. 12 'INCOME TAX' contains exactly one section, '39-12-101. Preemption by state.' Wyoming's personal tax burden is sales and use tax (Title 39, ch. 15 and ch. 16) and property tax (ch. 13). Federal income tax withholding is 26 U.S.C. ch. 24.

Federal, and largely preempted. Denied boarding, cancellation and delay compensation come from US DOT rules under 49 U.S.C. s 41712 (14 C.F.R. pt. 250, pt. 259), and the Airline Deregulation Act (49 U.S.C. s 41713) preempts state law on air-carrier prices, routes and services. Wyoming's Title 37 does carry carrier chapters - ch. 8 Motor Carriers, ch. 9 Railroads, ch. 11 Common Carriers by Air - but they are licensing and safety statutes and create no passenger compensation right; interstate motor-carrier and rail passenger matters are federal (49 U.S.C. subtits. IV-V). Nothing to list.

Federal, and constitutionally exclusive. U.S. Const. art. I, s 8, cl. 1 and s 10, cl. 2; the Tariff Act of 1930 and the Harmonized Tariff Schedule, 19 U.S.C. Wyoming has a Foreign Trade Zones chapter (Title 40, ch. 11) but it merely enables participation in the federal zone programme (19 U.S.C. s 81a et seq.) and levies nothing.

Federal. Immigration status and work authorisation are governed by the Immigration and Nationality Act, 8 U.S.C. ch. 12, with employer verification at 8 U.S.C. s 1324a. Wyoming has no work-permit statute; the only related state provision seen on the register is Title 42, ch. 12 (Citizens and Qualified Aliens Status Verification for Welfare), a benefits-eligibility check rather than a work permit.

register.name: D.C. Law Library - Code of the District of Columbia (Council of the District of Columbia, published with the non-profit Open Law Library)
register.access_notes: Reachable and fast. About 20 GET requests on 23 September 2026 from curl with an honest, self-identifying user-agent ('canon-legislation-indexer/1.0 (metadata indexing; contact ...)'), spaced roughly 2 seconds apart; no user-agent spoofing, no browser impersonation. Every request returned HTTP 200 on the first try; no 403, no 429, no bot challenge, no CAPTCHA at any point. Stable URL shape: /us/dc/council/code, /us/dc/council/code/titles/<n>, /us/dc/council/code/titles/<n>/chapters/<n>, and .../subchapters/<roman>. Title and chapter pages print the exact caption, the child subchapters or the section catchlines, and the section range; the Code table of contents page also prints the Publication Information block with the 'Current through' date. I fetched table-of-contents pages only - no section text pages - so no statute text was copied. TWO THINGS A HUMAN SHOULD WEIGH BEFORE ANY BULK USE: (1) every page footer says 'The codes and laws on this website are in the public domain. Please do not scrape. Instead, bulk download the HTML or XML.' (the bulk repositories are github.com/DCCouncil/law-html and github.com/DCCouncil/law-xml; neither carries a LICENSE file - the GitHub API reports license: null, default branch 'publication/2021-10-18'); (2) https://code.dccouncil.gov/robots.txt allows general crawling for '*' ('Allow: /') but sets 'Content-signal: search=yes,ai-train=no' and separately disallows named AI crawlers, including 'ClaudeBot', 'GPTBot', 'CCBot', 'Google-Extended', 'Applebot-Extended', 'Bytespider', 'Amazonbot' and 'meta-externalagent'. My fetches were made under the generic '*' group (Allow: /), were metadata-only, were not a crawl and were not for model training, but the site's stated preference is bulk download over page fetching and the ai-train signal is 'no'. Curiosity worth recording: the D.C. Law Library also carries 941 'Federal Laws Codified in the D.C. Code' and 15 'Laws of the United Kingdom Codified in the D.C. Code'.

licence.summary: Open. The Council's own site states flatly that the material is in the public domain, on every page footer, and offers bulk HTML and XML downloads - so reuse AND adaptation are permitted. This matches the US government edicts doctrine (Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org, 590 U.S. 255 (2020)): the text of the D.C. Code as enacted by the Council is not copyrightable. No attribution condition, no non-commercial condition and no share-alike condition is stated anywhere on the register. Two caveats a human should keep in mind. First, the site pairs the public-domain statement with a request - 'Please do not scrape. Instead, bulk download the HTML or XML.' - which is a conduct request rather than a copyright restriction, and its robots.txt disallows named AI crawlers and signals ai-train=no (see access_notes). Second, the free Council/Open Law Library edition at code.dccouncil.gov is the unannotated text; the printed and commercially-hosted ANNOTATED 'D.C. Official Code' is produced by a commercial publisher under contract with the Council, and that publisher's annotations, notes and editorial apparatus carry the publisher's own copyright even though the statutory text does not. Which publisher holds that contract today was NOT verified in this session - check before reusing anything from an annotated edition.
licence.attribution: None required by the register. Courtesy citation: Code of the District of Columbia, D.C. Law Library, Council of the District of Columbia (code.dccouncil.gov).
licence.quote: The codes and laws on this website are in the public domain.

acts.title: Code of the District of Columbia, Title 32 (Labor), Chapter 1 - Displaced Workers Protection
acts.identifier: D.C. Code tit. 32, ch. 1 (ss 32-101 to 32-111.07); Subchapter I [General], ss 32-101 to 32-103
acts.verified_how: fetched https://code.dccouncil.gov/us/dc/council/code/titles/32/chapters/1: breadcrumb 'Title 32. Labor. / Chapter 1. Displaced Workers Protection.' with 'Subchapter I. [General]. ss 32-101 - 32-103' and 'Subchapter II. Protections for Workers Displaced by COVID-19. ss 32-111.01 - 32-111.07'; I also opened Subchapter I (https://code.dccouncil.gov/us/dc/council/code/titles/32/chapters/1/subchapters/I), which lists 's 32-101. Covered employees.', 's 32-102. Transition employment period.' and 's 32-103. Enforcement.'. Not marked '[Repealed]' or '[Not Funded]' (the register marks both inline, e.g. 'Chapter 5A. Freedom to Contract Within the Broadcast Industry. [Repealed]' in the same title). Currency: the Code's Publication Information block reads 'Current through Sept. 5, 2026', 'Last codified D.C. Law: Law 26-177 effective Sept. 5, 2026', 'Last codified Emergency Law: Act 26-416 effective Aug. 13, 2026', 'Last codified Federal Law: Public Law 115-334 approved Dec. 20, 2018'.
acts.notes: READ THE SCOPE CAREFULLY. This is the closest thing the District has to a general termination statute, but it is narrow: it protects service-contract and building-service employees when a contract or a building changes hands, by requiring a transition employment period, and Subchapter II adds COVID-era re-hire rights. The District has NO general severance-pay statute and NO mini-WARN mass-layoff notice statute - federal WARN (29 U.S.C. ss 2101-2109) does that work - and District employment is otherwise at-will. Final wages on discharge are governed by s 32-1303 in the wage chapter listed under Payroll/wages. If the corpus wants only general-application termination law, treat this topic as a gap instead.

Federal. Immigration status and work authorisation are governed by the Immigration and Nationality Act, 8 U.S.C. ch. 12 (employment authorisation and employer verification at 8 U.S.C. s 1324a).
